factual_claims.claim: Transformers have quadratic attention-prefill compute and linearly growing KV-cache memory, whereas fixed-state alternatives can lose capability and remain inefficient on GPU decode.
Mamba-3 is an inference-first state-space architecture that changes recurrence, state update, and I/O structure.
Mamba-3 uses exponential-trapezoidal recurrence with a learned trap gate, a complex update with data-dependent rotations, and a rank-4 MIMO path intended to raise arithmetic intensity.
Models from 180M through 1.5B are pretrained on 100B FineWeb-Edu tokens with the Llama-3.1 tokenizer and 2K context.
At 1.5B, Mamba-3 MIMO has 10.24 perplexity and 57.6 average accuracy, against Transformer 10.51/55.4, Mamba-2 10.47/55.7, and Gated DeltaNet 10.45/55.8.
On three formal state-tracking tasks, Mamba-3 scores 100.0, 98.51, and 87.75 percent, compared with Mamba-2 at 0.9, 47.81, and 0.88 percent.
For BF16 H100 kernel latency at state size 128, Mamba-3 SISO takes 0.156 ms per token, Mamba-2 takes 0.203 ms, and Mamba-3 MIMO takes 0.179 ms; MIMO is the stronger quality point.

factual_claims.claim: Pure Mamba-3 is weaker on some semi-structured and unstructured retrieval tasks, motivating hybrid attention for sparse-fact retention.
factual_claims.support: direct, with motivation bounded to the chip's stated recovery mechanism

factual_claims.claim: The reported results jointly support improved language-model quality and recurrent inference efficiency, with a SISO/MIMO quality-latency tradeoff.

caveats: The abstract does not claim that 1.5B evidence transfers to 7B.
The final synthesis is limited to the reported architecture and experiments.
Retrieval weakness is preserved rather than suppressed.
